text:
mina: quick heads-up — hit a terse but reproducible leak in the Go generator pull iterator when auth refresh races ctx cancel.

jord: can you paste a tiny repro + what you saw vs expected?

mina: expected: Next(ctx) returns and all SDK goroutines stop. observed: Next returns, iter.Err shows deadline, but auth refresh goroutine keeps logging retries. Happens if refresh takes longer than ctx deadline.

ash: which API pattern? Pull-style iterator with Next(ctx)?

mina: yes. minimal sketch: `ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 700*time.Millisecond); iter, _ := client.Generator(ctx, req); for iter.Next(ctx) { _ = iter.Token() }`. After cancel, logs show repeated "auth: refresh start".

jord: sounds like either transport retry or auth helper started work without honoring ctx. Two actionable items: (1) add Close() to iterator so callers can explicitly stop internals; (2) make auth refresh cancellation-aware.

ash: agree. Close() is low-risk and improves DX quickly. We should also update sampleapp quickstart to use `defer iter.Close()` so new users learn the pattern.

mina: local workaround I used: create a child context for iterator and cancel it on exit, but that's ugly. Example: `opCtx, stop := context.WithCancel(ctx); iter, _ := client.Generator(opCtx, req); defer stop()` — works but not ideal to teach.

jord: test plan: add a unit test with a fake slow auth provider that sleeps during refresh, cancel after first token, then assert no auth goroutines remain after a short grace period. Make it eventual-assertion to avoid flakes.

ci-bot: opened issue #2931 "go-sdk: add Iterator.Close() and make auth refresh ctx-aware" assigned to @jord.

mina: I'll PR the sampleapp change + flaky-resistant test. jord: want to own the iterator API patch?

jord: yes — I'll prototype io.Closer on the iterator, make Close idempotent, and update docs. Will also run a quick middleware audit for other detached goroutines.

ash: thanks for the clear repro, mina. this will save support tickets. :+1:
